application.name: ofetch
application.summary: ofetch is a TypeScript HTTP client library that wraps the Fetch API with a higher-level request pipeline. It adds typed response parsing, option merging, lifecycle hooks, retries, timeouts, normalized errors, and Node.js-specific fetch integration.
application.purpose: Provide a lightweight, type-friendly $fetch/ofetch abstraction for making HTTP requests consistently across browser-like and Node.js runtimes while simplifying common concerns such as JSON bodies, query parameters, retries, and error handling.

domains.name: Core HTTP client API
domains.description: The public $fetch/ofetch callable, raw-response API, hook execution, and configured fetch instance factory.

domains.name: Request construction
domains.description: Option/default merging, URL base/query composition, HTTP method classification, header handling, and request body serialization.

domains.name: Response parsing
domains.description: Selection and application of response parsers such as JSON, text, blob, arrayBuffer, and stream based on options or content type.

domains.name: Error handling
domains.description: Normalization of failed requests into FetchError objects carrying request, response, status, and parsed error data.

domains.name: Retry and timeout
domains.description: Automatic retry behavior for selected HTTP status codes, retry delays, abort signals, and timeout-driven cancellation.

domains.name: Node.js runtime integration
domains.description: Node-specific fetch selection and optional keep-alive HTTP/HTTPS agent configuration.

domains.name: Examples and tests
domains.description: Demonstration scripts, playground code, and test helpers that exercise the library behavior.

applicationFacts: The library exports browser-like entry points from src/index.ts and Node-specific entry points from src/node.ts.
The core createFetch factory creates a $fetch callable with raw, native, and create helper methods.
$fetch returns parsed response data, while $fetch.raw returns the full FetchResponse object.
Request options are merged with global defaults, including deep merging of query/params and headers.
POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE are treated as payload methods; request bodies on these methods may be automatically JSON-stringified.
For JSON-serializable payload bodies, content-type and accept headers default to application/json when not already set.
Response parsing can be explicitly selected with responseType or parseResponse, or inferred from the Content-Type header.
JSON responses are parsed with destr by default, with parseResponse available as an override.
Responses with status 101, 204, 205, or 304, as well as HEAD requests, are treated as having no body to parse.
Automatic retries are governed by retry options, retryDelay, and retryStatusCodes; default retry-eligible statuses include 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504.
When retry is not explicitly numeric, non-payload methods default to one retry and payload methods default to zero retries.
Timeouts are implemented with AbortController and produce a TimeoutError-style abort reason.
Lifecycle hooks can be supplied individually or as arrays and are awaited sequentially.
HTTP responses with 4xx or 5xx status throw a normalized FetchError unless ignoreResponseError is enabled.
The Node entry point can use keep-alive HTTP/HTTPS agents when FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE is enabled.
Build configuration targets src/index and src/node with declaration generation and CommonJS emission.
